Term1: ORZID2 GMENU SEPSIS SEVERE BETA-LACTAM REACTION
Text:
## TREATMENT OF SEPSIS WITH SEVERE BETA-LACTAM REACTION
[For more info, refer to Assessment of Beta-Lactam Reaction document [CLICK HERE]](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)
## The following regimen(s) should only be used if the patient has a history of a
## severe reaction to a Beta-Lactam antimicrobial including but not limited to:
Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN)
Anaphylaxis
Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
Generalized exanthematous pustulosis
Hemolytic anemia
Immune hepatitis
Interstitial nephritis
Mucosal, cardiovascular, or respiratory system involvement
Reaction needed medical intervention
Skin desquamation
Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS)
Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN)
## Treatment
[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h](psjizid-levofloxacin-iv-750mg-q24h-sepsis)
## Recent MRSA isolate
[<ADD> Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h to above regimen](orz-set-abx-vanco-sepsis-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)
## Clinically unstable (ICU level care/hypotensive/tachycardic) AND recent multi-
## drug resistant gram-negative rod isolate
[<ADD> Tobramycin 5 mg/kg IV x 1 dose to above regimen](psjizid-tobramycin-5-mg-kg-iv-sepsis)
*If CrCl less than 50 ml/min: 2 mg/kg x 1 dose (use order above and modify dose)
-Pharmacy to follow
